title: Parallax Write Instruction (m-unit-work)
description: The canonical, language-neutral write-instruction vocabulary a unit of work buffers and flushes (m-unit-work) — the write-side analogue of `object-query.schema.json`. A write from any frontend lowers into exactly one keyed, predicate, or caller-addressed (target) instruction. Valid-Time input is spelled `validFrom`; a bounded `*Until` operation additionally carries `until`, so its window is `[validFrom, until)`. The finite Transaction-Time instant is Clock context supplied at flush and is not an instruction member. The framework-owned optimistic observation is likewise flush-time context: `observedVersion`, `observedTxStart` and `observedValidStart` are forbidden on durable rows. There are no business/processing aliases. SERDE ROUND-TRIP CONTRACT: a conforming implementation MUST round-trip every instruction through this canonical form losslessly — `serialize(deserialize(x)) == x` (JSON and YAML).

keyedWriteInstruction.description: A keyed write: a mutation on one entity carrying flat attribute-named rows, authorized by the source the write was stated through — a read's evidence or an admitted insertion — never by a condition of its own. A Valid-Time mutation carries `validFrom`; the bounded `*Until` forms additionally carry `until`.

rows.description: The neutral write input: one or more flat attribute-named rows the mutation operates on (`$defs/writeRow`). A generating implementation classifies each field by metamodel role and derives the emitted column list and ORDER by filtering the target's Entity Layout slots. A keyed instruction on a TEMPORAL target (one whose inheritance family derives an As-Of Axis — a descendant inherits the root's declaration unchanged and declares none of its own, m-inheritance) carries EXACTLY ONE row (`m-unit-work` "A temporal keyed instruction carries exactly one row"): each row closes its own milestone, consumes its own Temporal Observation, and chains its own successors, and a temporal entity never collapses into a set-based statement (`m-batch-write`), so several rows are several chains that must be authored as several instructions. That bound is MODEL-dependent — whether the target is temporal is not visible here — so this array states the general one-or-more shape and the temporal singleton is enforced against the metamodel.

validFrom.description: The Valid-Time lower bound of the mutation (`from_z`). Required on every bounded `*Until` mutation.

until.description: The exclusive Valid-Time upper bound of a bounded `*Until` mutation (`thru_z`), always paired with `validFrom`.

allOf.description: A bounded `*Until` mutation is over `[validFrom, until)`, so it must carry both Valid-Time bounds; a plain mutation must omit `until`.

predicateWriteInstruction.description: A predicate-selected (set-based) write: a mutation on every row of `target.entity` matching `target.predicate`, with `assignments` on an amendment and a `row` on a replacement. An empty `assignments` list is the empty amendment, judged like any other and then dropped, with no statement. A replacement's `row` states each selected object's complete writable state, completed when the write is prepared exactly as any replacement's is; a primary-key member it states addresses nothing, since the predicate selects the rows, and is never written. This is the set-based analogue of the keyed instruction. It lowers to one readless statement, so its target is an unversioned non-temporal Entity; a model-aware validator refuses any other target (`m-batch-write`). Assignment list order and row member order are DATA order only — the target's Entity Layout determines the emitted SET columns and their binds.

allOf.description: An amendment (`amend`) MUST carry `assignments`, possibly empty, and no `row`.
A replacement (`replace`) MUST carry `row`, possibly empty, and no `assignments`.

targetWriteInstruction.description: A caller-addressed (target) write of the one existing `entity` object its `row` names by primary key, under the starting revision its caller states: an amendment (`amend` / `amendUntil`), a complete replacement (`replace` / `replaceUntil`), a deletion (`delete`), or a termination (`terminate` / `terminateUntil`). The row's primary-key members address the object and are no assignment; an amendment's other members are its assignments, a replacement's are the object's complete writable state, and a destructive write's row names the key alone. The revision is a member of its own, never a row member, and every target write states exactly one: `ifVersion` for a versioned target, or `ifTxStart` — the observed milestone's Transaction-Time start, never the writing transaction's own instant — for a temporal one. An unversioned Non-Temporal target has no revision to state, so it takes no caller-addressed write. Which revision a target takes, whether it admits the verb, and whether it requires `validFrom` depend on the model and are judged when the write is prepared.

ifVersion.description: The version a versioned target's caller last observed the object at.

ifTxStart.description: The Transaction-Time start of the milestone a temporal target's caller last observed.

validFrom.description: The Valid-Time instant a Bitemporal target write starts at (`from_z`), which need not be the stored rectangle's own start. Required on every bounded `*Until` write.

until.description: The exclusive Valid-Time upper bound of a bounded target write (`thru_z`), always paired with `validFrom`.

oneOf.description: A versioned target's stated starting version.
A temporal target's stated starting milestone.

allOf.description: A bounded target write is over `[validFrom, until)`, so it must carry both Valid-Time bounds; unbounded forms must omit `until`.

writeTarget.description: The exact entity a predicate-selected write begins from plus its `m-predicate` predicate. A set-based write selects rows and shapes no result, so its selection is exactly the Predicate grammar — ordering, the cap, Temporal Selections, result narrowing, and Includes are Object Query clauses and have no spelling here at all. The descriptor-dependent scope rules are validated separately.

writeAssignment.description: One ordered predicate-write assignment. Model-aware elaboration resolves `attr`, then decodes each non-null declared scalar leaf exactly once with m-wire — each element of a scalar collection's array alike. Nullability, a scalar collection's whole array, and complete Value Object document carriers remain structural rules; this schema intentionally does not duplicate per-type literal grammar. Duplicate and unassignable references are rejected by model-aware validation.

writeRow.description: A flat attribute-named durable write row. Every key is an Entity Attribute or top-level Value Object name, never a physical column. The framework-owned optimistic observations `observedVersion`, `observedTxStart` and `observedValidStart` are attached only at flush and are forbidden here. Scalar fields carry neutral literals or DB-computed markers, a scalar collection field its whole ordered array of neutral literals, and Value Object fields their complete ordered document value.

not.description: The framework-owned optimistic observation is not durable instruction state: neither `observedVersion` nor either half of the observed milestone's own coordinate (`observedTxStart` / `observedValidStart`) may ride on a durable row.

writeRowValue.description: The structural value a neutral write-row field carries, classified by its resolved Entity Layout contributor rather than by carrier shape. Model-aware elaboration decodes each non-null scalar leaf exactly once with m-wire; a Value Object remains its whole object or array document and DB-computed markers retain their role-owned meaning. This schema intentionally does not duplicate per-type literal grammar.

anyOf.description: A value-object document (m-value-object): a value-object-named field binds the WHOLE embedded composite atomically as one document value in its Storage Layout position — a JSON object for a `one` value object, a JSON array of objects for a `many` one. A scalar-collection-named field (m-metamodel) binds its whole ordered array of neutral literals the same way, each element decoded once with m-wire.

writeComputedMarker.description: A one-key DB-COMPUTED marker in a neutral write row: the attribute's value is derived by the database rather than authored as a literal bind, so the generating implementation emits the strategy's SQL fragment. Applies ONLY to a scalar-attribute column (a value-object column's value is always the literal document even when marker-shaped, disambiguated by metamodel role, not by shape).

computed.description: The pk-gen `max` strategy: the column is emitted as `coalesce(max(col), ?) + ?` — the computation folds into the INSERT's SQL, so a `max`-strategy insert stays statically derivable.

increment.description: A self-referential advance emitted as `col = col + ?` (e.g. a sequence registry's `next_val`); the integer is the amount added.

instant.description: A finite Valid-Time instant, spelled as `m-wire`'s `timestamp` and decoded by that codec. No authored bound is infinite: an unbounded write omits `until`, and the `infinity` literal is refused.

entityName.description: The concrete descriptor entity a write begins from, spelled bare or namespace-qualified (identity.schema.json).

keyedMutation.description: The keyed write mutation surface: `insert` opens a row, `amend` assigns the members its row names, `replace` states the object's complete writable state, and `delete` / `terminate` end it, plus the full-bitemporal bounded rectangle forms (`insertUntil` / `amendUntil` / `replaceUntil` / `terminateUntil`). `compatibility-case.schema.json`'s buffered keyed write references this enum rather than redefining it.

targetMutation.description: The caller-addressed (target) write mutation surface: the amendment `amend`, the complete `replace`, the physical `delete` of a Non-Temporal object, and the milestone-closing `terminate` of a temporal one, each with its bounded `*Until` form where one exists. `compatibility-case.schema.json`'s caller-addressed entries reference this enum rather than redefining it.

predicateMutation.description: The predicate-selected (set-based) write mutation surface: `amend`, `replace`, and `delete`. Its target is unversioned and Non-Temporal, so it has no history to close and no Valid Time to bound: no `terminate` and no bounded `*Until` form. A set-based write has no `insert` form — there is no predicate to select rows that do not yet exist. `compatibility-case.schema.json`'s `predicateWrite` references this enum rather than redefining it.
